fact_check.claim: 2026-27 aid-office table: $96,318 billed, $3,416 non-billed, $99,734 total
fact_check.note: The numbers are on the page, but under tables labeled 2025-26; the 'Undergraduate Estimated Cost of Attendance - 2026-27' heading has column labels and no values. Tuition $73,946 and housing $13,744 are confirmed as 2026-27 by other official pages, so the figures are probably right, but the article states 'for 2026-27, the aid office's table lists' as if the page said so.

fact_check.claim: Tuition $73,946 is the 2026-27 endowed-college rate
fact_check.note: Endowed college tuition 2026-27 is $73,946 (3.76% increase).

fact_check.claim: Mandatory fees $1,024 = $424 student activity fee + $600 Cornell Health fee
fact_check.note: Fee breakdown matches (page table is labeled 2025-26).

fact_check.claim: Housing double $13,744; Food Unlimited $7,604; books $1,234; personal $2,182
fact_check.note: Match the page. Housing page confirms $6,872 x 2 = $13,744 for 2026-27; meal plan page confirms $7,604 Unlimited.

fact_check.claim: Transportation 'varies by region'
fact_check.note: Page says varies by region.

fact_check.claim: Families up to $75,000 with typical assets: grants, scholarships and work-study cover full cost of attendance
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Families up to $125,000 with typical assets get grant/scholarship aid that covers tuition
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Most families up to $75,000 have $0 expected contributions, $0 loans, and a typical $5,000 work-study award
fact_check.note: Page says families up to $75,000 with typical assets get $0 student and parent contribution, no loans, and a $5,000 work-study award. It does not say 'most' or 'typical' work-study.
Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Student Health Insurance is an optional cost that loans can finance
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Cornell Student Health Plan $4,092 for 12 months, about $341 a month
fact_check.note: Page says $4,092 for 12 months; billed by term ($2,046 fall, $2,046 spring for 7/1-6/30 coverage). 4,092/12 = 341.

fact_check.claim: Fall 2026 waiver deadline July 31, 2026; waivers approved every semester; spring reverification due January 31, 2027; after deadline only prorated refund request
fact_check.note: Confirmed. Spring new matriculated students have an earlier deadline of January 21, 2027 (not mentioned; optional). Refund is via a termination-of-coverage request.

fact_check.claim: Double room $6,872 per semester
fact_check.note: Fall 2026 and Spring 2027 each $6,872.

fact_check.claim: Co-op double $3,487 to $4,981 a semester
fact_check.note: Range confirmed; rates vary by house.

fact_check.claim: Bear Basic $4,978 a year vs $7,604 Unlimited, offered as a cheaper lever for full-pay students (article says it assumes on-campus dining)
fact_check.note: Prices are right ($2,489/semester; $3,802 Unlimited per semester), but Bear Basic is only available to on-campus undergraduates who enrolled before Summer 2021 and to students living off campus. Presenting it as a lever for an on-campus student is wrong.

fact_check.claim: Non-aided students saw tuition rise $1,806 to $2,680 for 2026-27
fact_check.note: Confirmed.

fact_check.claim: Grad Ithaca 2026-27: fees $701, housing $19,962, food $5,768, books $2,464, transportation $3,754, personal $4,196, non-billed subtotal $36,144
fact_check.note: All confirmed. Fees are $110 activity + $580 Cornell Health. 36,144/12 = 3,012; 36,845/12 = 3,070.

fact_check.claim: Stipend minimums effective Aug 21, 2026: $36,684 (9 months), $48,912 (12-month assistantship), $44,463 (12-month fellowship)
Registered PhD students and graduate assistants get free TCAT OmniRide passes
fact_check.note: Quoted on page.

fact_check.claim: Students enrolled a year or more ride free after 6 p.m. weekdays and all weekend; standard pass $200 a year
fact_check.note: Confirmed; rate shown at purchase.

fact_check.claim: Hayden Watkins '28 (Student Assembly VP finance) said his family had to do 'financial gymnastics' even with aid; placed in the full-pay scenario
fact_check.note: Quote is real ('some financial gymnastics, even with aid') but it is about an aided student, so placing it in the full-pay paragraph is misleading, and that sentence carries no link.

fact_check.claim: Carlin Reyen estimated $450 a year for books, hasn't bought books since first semester; Anabel's Grocery in Anabel Taylor Hall accepts SNAP
fact_check.note: Page says she hasn't paid for books since her first-year writing seminar and estimated about $450 a year otherwise; Anabel's accepts SNAP.

fact_check.claim: Aid office contact 607-255-5145, finaid@cornell.edu; aid can't cover deposit or rent in unregistered months; choose housing costing less over 12 months than the off-campus budget
fact_check.note: All confirmed.
All recomputed and correct.

fact_check.claim: Grad nine-month stipend leaves 'about $1,000 a month above the estimate' (first margin)
fact_check.note: $36,684 is paid over nine months, but the $3,070 estimate is a 12-month cost. Spread over 12 months a nine-month stipend is $3,057, below the estimate. The $1,000 margin holds only for the 12-month assistantship.

beats_top.query: cornell student budget by scenario low income student costs beyond tuition
beats_top.why: College Factual gives average net price by income band and a loan-payment projection (with a negative net price artifact), and no monthly budget by situation. Ours gives four scenarios with sourced 2026-27 numbers and what to do; it will be clearly better once the mismatches are fixed.
changes: Fix the Bear Basic and 2026-27 labeling errors so the numbers can be trusted
Make the grad nine-month versus 12-month comparison correct
Add a one-line monthly total per scenario near the top so a student sees their number at once

fixes: In the lede and the 'How we built these' paragraph, stop saying the aid office's table 'lists' 2026-27 figures. Say the aid page's cost table is labeled 2025-26 with an empty 2026-27 table, and that we treat $73,946 tuition and $13,744 housing as 2026-27 because the trustees' announcement (https://news.cornell.edu/stories/2026/03/board-trustees-approves-2026-27-budget-parameters) and the housing rates page confirm them. Also relabel the figure title 'Undergraduate cost of attendance, endowed colleges, 2026-27' to say the books, personal and fee lines come from the aid page's table labeled 2025-26 and are unconfirmed for 2026-27.

In the full-pay scenario, delete the Bear Basic comparison, or state that Bear Basic ($4,978 a year; https://scl.cornell.edu/residential-life/dining/meal-plans-rates/undergraduate-meal-plans) is open only to on-campus undergraduates who enrolled before Summer 2021 and to students living off campus, so it is not an option for a typical on-campus student.

Move the Hayden Watkins 'financial gymnastics' sentence out of the full-pay scenario (he was describing a family with aid), put it in the partial-aid scenario with the Sun link https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2025/09/financial-gymnastics-cornell-s-cost-of-attendance-surpasses-100k-for-some-students-in-2025-2026, and keep the phrase 'some financial gymnastics, even with aid' accurate.

In Scenario 1, remove 'most' and 'typical' from 'most families ... a typical $5,000 work-study award'. Write that families with income up to $75,000 and typical assets get $0 expected contributions, no loans and a $5,000 work-study award (https://finaid.cornell.edu/affordability).

In Scenario 4, correct the nine-month stipend comparison: $36,684 over nine months is $4,076 a month, but spread over 12 months it is $3,057, which is about $13 a month below the $3,070 estimate. State the roughly $1,000 monthly margin only for the 12-month assistantship ($48,912) and keep the fellowship margin of about $635.

In the Where budgets break, health-plan item, add that spring new matriculated students have an earlier waiver deadline of January 21, 2027 (https://studenthealthbenefits.cornell.edu/node/179), and say the refund after the deadline requires a termination of coverage request.
